name: Research
one_line: Files produced by doing research: a named project's manuscripts, abstracts, protocols, figures, datasets and lab records, plus the venue and lab context that explains them.
design_cite: "Research files may use project, stage, artifact type, lab, and venue"; launch scope: "academic coursework, college applications, research and lab work, career and recruiting, photos and captures, and code projects"; default order: "a Research template may define project → stage → artifact type"

node_test.why: Three of the five keys (stage, lab, venue) are referenced by no other roster schema, and the two that are shared (project, artifact_type) are shared with code by canonical reference, which is what makes shares_field derived rather than a reason to merge. The set is five, inside 00's "usually three to six that may help build a future folder proposal". No child schema is proposed for any artifact type: manuscript, abstract, protocol, figure and dataset are VALUES of artifact_type.

fields.rule_family: project-identifier token co-occurring with research-artifact context (an abstract heading, a numbered-protocol + materials structure, a figure-caption sequence, or a manuscript title block) in a filename, title, or page-one heading zone
fields.why: 00: "Research files may use project, stage, artifact type, lab, and venue", and the group seed sentence supplies the pattern this rule family confirms: "For a research group, it might be a manuscript, abstract, or protocol with a known project identifier". A labelled slot (a spreadsheet cell headed Project, an IRB form's Protocol Title field) reaches direct instead, per 00's direct-fact rule for "a labeled form field"; the pattern-plus-context path is what the deterministic signals below actually implement.

fields.rule_family: submission-lifecycle term pattern (cover letter, response to reviewers, revision, proof, camera-ready) co-occurring with manuscript or venue evidence in the same document or in an archive manifest
fields.why: 00: "Research files may use project, stage, artifact type, lab, and venue". The ceiling is validated only on the lifecycle-term path; ordinary prose stage evidence (a body sentence saying the reviewers' comments have been addressed) is llm_supported, which is why stage sits in needs_llm as well. A version number or a v7 filename suffix is NOT stage evidence: 00's narrow-date rule warns about "numbers that look like years but are course identifiers, version numbers, build numbers, ZIP codes, or other unrelated values", and a version family is a universal fact, not a workflow position.

fields.rule_family: artifact term pattern confirmed by document structure (abstract heading; numbered steps plus a materials list; a figure-caption sequence; a header row over sample-shaped columns; slide titles plus speaker notes)
fields.why: 00: "Research files may use project, stage, artifact type, lab, and venue". Members are values discovered at runtime, never roster nodes. Structure is what confirms the term: 00 requires extractors to preserve the difference between a heading, a table label, a filename and ordinary body text, and presentations to yield "slide titles, text boxes, speaker notes where available".

fields.rule_family: organization gazetteer (R4's content) matched at word boundaries with positional weighting, PLUS a research-role context term in the same zone; a bare organization hit is struck by the never-alone rule
fields.why: 00: "Research files may use project, stage, artifact type, lab, and venue". The role requirement is 00's own: "Columbia can appear as an authoring school, course provider, target institution, employer, research venue, or merely a cited organization" — research venue is named in that list, so an institution string carries no role until context supplies one. Word boundaries are required because "It should use word-boundary matching rather than substring matching". See open_question: a lab named after its PI is one step from authorship-as-destination.

fields.rule_family: venue gazetteer (R4's content) matched at word boundaries in a high-weight zone — filename, title, page-one heading, cover-letter salutation, or an editorial email's subject — and never from a hit whose only occurrence is in the reference_list zone
fields.why: 00: "Research files may use project, stage, artifact type, lab, and venue". The zone restriction is 00's positional-weighting rule stated for exactly this failure: "A course code or university name found in a filename, title, or page-one heading is more meaningful than the same text appearing once in a reference list on page eighteen". A journal name in a bibliography describes a cited work, not this artifact.

Search, explanation and residual-routing field only, not one of the 3–6 folder-level fields. Research needs it because the discrimination that sends a PDF to Reading Inbox rather than into a project is authorship: whether the paper is the holder's own output or somebody else's reading material. 00 forbids it as a folder level outright — "It should avoid using authorship or creator identity as a destination dimension" — and warns that document metadata author fields "may be stale, generic, or generated by a tool rather than a person", so a direct read of a DOCX core property is still supporting evidence about the file, never a destination.

deterministic: a research-artifact structure (an abstract heading; numbered protocol steps beside a materials list; a manuscript title block over sectioned body text; a figure-caption sequence) co-occurring with a project-identifier token in the filename, title, or page-one heading zone

a labelled slot in a structured source naming the project, protocol title, PI or department — a spreadsheet cell under a Project header, a DOCX table cell, an IRB form field — which is 00's "labeled form field" direct-fact path
a submission-lifecycle term (cover letter, response to reviewers, revision, proof) co-occurring with manuscript or venue evidence in the same document or in an archive manifest

an archive manifest whose member names combine a manuscript, figures, supplementary material and a cover letter, read without unpacking — 00: "the normal scan should never extract archive contents to the filesystem"
a venue gazetteer hit at a word boundary in a filename, title, page-one heading, or an editorial email's subject line, where that hit is not confined to the reference_list zone

a repository-marker check that runs BEFORE research is admitted on a code_structured file, because 00 puts that evidence on the code side: "Code-related files should rely heavily on local structural evidence, including repository roots and package files"
needs_llm: stage read from unlabelled prose — a sentence saying the reviewers' comments have been addressed, or that this is the final version for typesetting — where no lifecycle term pattern fires; 00 names this the LLM's job: "interpret an unusual research artifact"
an OCR'd notebook or whiteboard page whose only structure is handwriting: a lab record, a lecture note, or a personal list
whether an image is a research figure at all — 00: an opaque image "may be a screenshot of a receipt, application portal, conversation, code error, or research figure"
whether a project or venue token names the holder's own work or one merely cited or attended, which is the role question the gazetteer cannot answer
whether a heterogeneous archive is a submission packet (one venue, one manuscript) or an unrelated download bundle
never_alone: a DOI, a journal name, or a citation string alone — the downloaded paper Ravikumar_2019_NatureMethods.pdf carries all three and is reading material, which is why 00 gives it a residual home: "papers, articles, reports, and saved PDFs that appear to be reading material but have no active research, course, or project association"
a lab, university or institute name alone — 00: "Columbia can appear as an authoring school, course provider, target institution, employer, research venue, or merely a cited organization"
the token 'lab' in a filename alone — Lab 4 writeup.docx is a course lab report and belongs to academic
a source_type alone: spreadsheet, code_structured, presentation, calendar and opaque_binary all appear in this domain and none of them proves it; the extension is a routing signal

a bare 4-digit number as a year or a project id — 00: "numbers that look like years but are course identifiers, version numbers, build numbers, ZIP codes, or other unrelated values"; in this domain it is just as likely a run number, a plate number or an instrument model
a filename alone on an unreadable instrument file — 00: "the system should not infer a purpose from their filename alone"

work_types_note: These are VALUES of the artifact_type field, discovered at runtime like any value; none of them is a roster node and none licenses a child schema.
grouping_reasons: one named project's artifacts across stages — 00's own seed: "For a research group, it might be a manuscript, abstract, or protocol with a known project identifier"
one manuscript's version family across drafts, the submission packet, the response to reviewers and the proofs
one submission packet: archive members plus the cover letter and the editorial correspondence that names the same manuscript id
one lab's shared protocols and instrument records reused across several projects

a sparse figure or unlabelled results file joins a project neighbourhood as a context-supported member without acquiring a project fact — 00: "The graph does not automatically copy those missing facts onto sparse files"

template.why: 00's own recommendation for this domain: "a Research template may define project → stage → artifact type", and the ordering rule that puts project first: "For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders" A stage such as revision, and an artifact type such as figure, are unintelligible without the project, which is the parent-makes-the-child-intelligible rule. lab and venue are legal facts here and are deliberately NOT dimensions in the default order — they belong to situations (a lab-shared protocol library, a venue-scoped conference bundle) that are separate template rows on this schema. The order is a recommendation the user may reverse, remove, add to, or flatten.

collides_with.signal: One evidence item — the vocabulary of lab, protocol, procedure, results, figure, report — supports both. The discriminator is which pattern the item sits beside: a course-code pattern with academic context puts the file on academic (00: a course fact needs "a course-code pattern together with academic context"), while a project identifier beside manuscript, abstract or protocol structure puts it here. Fixture: Lab 4 writeup.docx.

A project identifier in a source file or notebook supports both, because project is one canonical key referenced by both schemas. The discriminator is structural and belongs to code: 00 — "Code-related files should rely heavily on local structural evidence, including repository roots and package files". A repository root or package manifest above the file counts for code; a manuscript or protocol neighbourhood counts here. Fixture: analysis/train_eval.py.

A sponsor or institution gazetteer hit beside currency columns supports both. The discriminator is scope: an account-holder-scoped record (institution plus account type) is finance; a project-scoped budget or financial report carrying a project identifier and proposal structure is research. Fixture: PVA-RDP_budget_FY26_sponsor.xlsx. Finance is a safety domain, so on a genuine tie its protection path runs regardless of which schema wins the item.

also_holds_with.why: 00's own two-schema case, on disjoint evidence: "An academic abstract submitted as part of a university application can retain project = PVA/RDP and document type = abstract while also carrying purpose = university application and target university = UChicago." The same file is also 00's dual-group example: "a PVA/RDP abstract that is both a Research artifact and a supporting document in a UChicago application packet". Fixture: Abstract_PVA-RDP_UChicago.pdf.

A thesis or dissertation chapter carries school and term on degree-programme evidence and project, stage and artifact_type on its own research evidence — two disjoint evidence sets on one file, which is co-activation, not the collision above. The pair therefore carries both edges, and the collision above supplies the discriminating signal that licence requires.

A computational project's analysis notebook legitimately carries repository and programming_language from repo markers and project, stage and artifact_type from the manuscript neighbourhood it belongs to. The pair also collides on the project token alone, and the collision above carries the discriminating signal. shares_field between these two schemas (project, artifact_type) is derived from the canonical references and is never authored here.

Human-subjects research: a consent form, an IRB protocol naming a clinical procedure, or a participant dataset activates the medical safety placeholder for protection while the research fields stay legal on the file's research evidence. medical writes no field rows today (it is a field-less safety placeholder), so this edge changes what is protected, not what is extracted. Fixture: IRB_Protocol_PVA-RDP_2026_signed.pdf.

falls_through_to.why: 00 defines this residual against exactly this domain: papers "that appear to be reading material but have no active research, course, or project association". Fixture: Ravikumar_2019_NatureMethods.pdf.

00: "standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group" — a signed ethics-approval letter or a completed-training certificate with no project association. Fixtures: the approval letter shape, Lab meeting — Chen Lab.ics.
Instrument output with no extractor and password-protected data archives are common here, and 00 requires them to be represented rather than guessed at. Fixture: Run07_platereader.raw.

role_split.why: Same entity type, different role: the organization that PRODUCED the work versus the institution the holder attends. 00 names this ambiguity for the identical string — "Columbia can appear as an authoring school, course provider, target institution, employer, research venue, or merely a cited organization". Recorded as a finding: the canonical row for lab currently carries an empty role_split_with, and widening the canonical list is R1c's or Joseph's, never this node's.

Same entity type inside one schema, different role: the organization that PUBLISHED or hosted the artifact versus the one that produced it. A university press, an institute-hosted workshop, or a conference run by a society will hit the same orgs gazetteer for both. This is the intra-schema half of the split above and is why the venue rule family is zone-restricted while the lab rule family is context-restricted.

sensitivity_why: Not because research is inherently private, but because this domain routinely holds human-subjects material — consent forms, participant identifiers inside datasets, IRB records — alongside unpublished manuscripts and editorial correspondence, and 00 requires mail material to be handled "while treating addresses and message content as potentially sensitive". The value is 00's phrase and nothing more; a handling class is P7's and none is assigned here.
open_question: lab is destination_eligible on the canonical row, but a lab is very often named after its principal investigator, so a lab folder level can quietly become the authorship collector 00 forbids: "It should avoid using authorship or creator identity as a destination dimension." The default template above sidesteps this by not branching on lab, but a lab-shared-protocol template legitimately would. Joseph's call: does a PI-named lab count as an organization (a real dimension) or as creator identity (metadata only, expressed through the template's metadata_only mechanism)? Not resolved here — it decides someone's real folder structure.
